## Source-fidelity preflight — `source-fidelity-preflight-v10-functional-surface-geometry`

I built the full ledger against `input/disclosure.md` (the only affirmative inventor authority here; `input/conversation.md` truncates mid-sentence at "…through a network interface, but" and adds nothing beyond the disclosure, and `input/brief.md` was used only for title/applicant/inventor/priority/government-support formalities).

**Traced clean (representative):** branch-limit-below-sum premise, per-channel contactor + connector current sensor + control-pilot interface + local connector identifier, upstream branch current sensor as independent safety input, isolated local bus to interfaces and contactors, the four stored per-session values, the subtract-non-charging-load-and-safety-reserve → sustaining-then-deficit allocation, pilot send + connector verification, reduced pilot command → verification interval → one-at-a-time shedding in stored order until below limit, the three-part reclosure gate with randomized delay, leakage-threshold welded detection → inhibit others + local fault indicator, network interface / signed token / last accepted branch limit in nonvolatile memory / outage behavior / token expiry, tamper-evident meter sequence and upload, and the one-transition-at-a-time service-input mapping stored only on agreement. Claims 1–16 each map to an exact disclosure passage; no dependent claim introduces untraced matter.

**Figure briefs:** all shapes are generic outlines in briefs that declare the views schematic, with shape-neutral claims and description, so the square contactor, circular sensor, rounded-rectangle vehicle and block outlines are depiction conventions. The substantive topology that *is* verbalized — sensor in series interrupting the branch conductor, all three drops downstream of the branch sensor, bus not touching the non-charging load, connector current sensor downstream of the contactor and upstream of the vehicle connector, fault indicator outside the controller — each traces to an affirmative passage. No "by way of example"/"any closed outline" language leaked into the application text.

**Numerals:** all 25 entries are used, each denotes exactly one thing, and every numeral in a figure brief appears in the description and the ledger. No placeholders, drafting notes, or open alternatives remain. No section views, so no section-line designation check applies. Abstract is 146 words.

**One issue found:** claim 1 (and claim 11's method counterpart, plus the description) recites the controller coupled to the connector current sensors, but no figure depicts that coupling — FIG. 2's bus branches only to the control-pilot interface and the contactor. That is a 37 CFR 1.83(a) drawing/claim correspondence gap, not a source-fidelity violation, and the fix stays inside disclosed matter (the disclosure requires the controller to "verif[y] the resulting connector current with the corresponding current sensor").

input.summary: Full source ledger built and closed. Every limitation of claims 1-16, all 25 reference numerals and numbered parts, all four figure briefs (FIG. 1-4), the Brief Description entries, Summary, Detailed Description, Abstract and Title were traced item by item to affirmative USER passages in input/disclosure.md (input/conversation.md is truncated mid-sentence at "through a network interface, but" and adds nothing further; input/brief.md was used only for title, applicant, inventor, no-priority and no-government-support formalities). Traced and supported: the branch-limit-below-sum-of-ratings premise; per-channel contactor, connector current sensor, control-pilot interface and local connector identifier; branch current sensor measuring total current upstream of the connector contactors as an independent safety input; isolated local bus to the connector interfaces and contactors; the four stored per-session values (charging authorization, requested current, minimum sustaining current, energy-deficit value); per-interval subtraction of measured non-charging branch load and configurable safety reserve to obtain available charging current; sustaining-first then deficit-weighted distribution; pilot send plus connector-current verification; reduced pilot command, verification interval, and one-at-a-time opening in a stored shedding order until measured branch current is below the branch limit (claims 2 and 12 re-measurement is entailed by "one at a time ... until"); the three-part reclosure gate including randomized recovery delay; leakage-threshold welded-contactor recording with inhibition of the other contactors on the branch and operation of the local fault indicator; network interface, signed local authorization token and last accepted branch limit in nonvolatile memory, outage continuation, no new session without an unexpired token naming that connector, tamper-evident meter sequence and upload on return; and the service-input mapping by one low-energy pilot transition at a time stored only after the sensed channel agrees. No optional embodiment, variant, material, operating condition or asserted result in the description or figure briefs was left untraced. Figure briefs were checked against the depiction-convention rule: every outline is a generic empty rectangle, square, circle or rounded rectangle in views the briefs declare schematic, with the claims and description shape-neutral, and the only verbalized substantive topology (branch sensor in series interrupting the branch conductor, all three drops downstream of the branch sensor, bus not touching the non-charging load, connector current sensor downstream of the contactor and upstream of the vehicle connector, fault indicator outside the controller body, flow-chart decision branches) each traces to an affirmative disclosure passage; no "by way of example" or "any closed outline" broadening language appears in the application text. Numeral ledger is one-to-one and complete: all 25 numerals are used in a figure and in the description, none carries two meanings, and no drafting note, placeholder, open question, instruction or unresolved alternative remains. No section views exist, so no section-line designation consistency check applies. Abstract is 146 words. One finding is reported: claim 1 and claim 11, and the Detailed Description, recite the controller coupled to the connector current sensors, but FIG. 2 shows the isolated local bus branching only to the control-pilot interface and the contactor, so no drawing depicts that claimed coupling; this is a 37 CFR 1.83(a) drawing-to-claim correspondence gap rather than a source-fidelity defect, and the supplied fix stays wholly within disclosed matter.

findings.title: Claimed coupling of the controller to the connector current sensors is not depicted in any figure
findings.where: figures/FIG-2.md (isolated local bus paragraph); draft/09-claims.md claim 1 third element and claim 11 verifying step; draft/08-detailed-description.md, FIG. 2 paragraph
findings.detail: Claim 1 requires "a controller coupled to the control-pilot interfaces of the plurality of connector channels, to the connector current sensors of the plurality of connector channels, to the contactors ... and to the branch current sensor", and the description asserts the same coupling for connector current sensor 124. The couplings to the control-pilot interfaces, to the contactors and to the branch current sensor are each depicted (FIG. 2 bus branches; FIG. 1 dashed sensing line to edge controller 106; FIG. 3 lines crossing the lower side of the large rectangle). The coupling to the connector current sensor is depicted nowhere: FIG. 2's bus "branches two ways" only, and circle 124 is touched by nothing except the power run it straddles. FIG. 1 and FIG. 3 contain no connector current sensor at all. A claimed feature therefore appears in no drawing (37 CFR 1.83(a)), and the FIG. 2 brief is internally out of step with the description paragraph that says the controller is coupled to sensor 124. This is a drawing-completeness defect, not an unsupported assertion: the disclosure affirmatively requires the coupling ("verifies the resulting connector current with the corresponding current sensor"; "A contactor is not reclosed until its connector current sensor reports zero"), so the correction adds no matter beyond the source.
findings.evidence: FIG-2.md: "A solid horizontal line enters from the left of the drawing area and crosses the left side of the dashed rectangle in its lower region, as the isolated local bus. Inside the rectangle it branches two ways: one branch continues right, below the corner and below the horizontal run, to the left side of the control-pilot interface block; the other rises, left of the incoming supply line, to the left side of the square outline of the contactor." | draft/08-detailed-description.md: "The isolated local bus 108 couples the edge controller 106 to the contactor 122 and the control-pilot interface 126 of the first connector channel 120. The edge controller 106 is also coupled to the connector current sensor 124 of that connector channel." | draft/09-claims.md claim 1: "a controller coupled to the control-pilot interfaces of the plurality of connector channels, to the connector current sensors of the plurality of connector channels, ..." | Inventor support for the coupling existing: disclosure.md "The controller sends each assigned limit through the control-pilot interface and verifies the resulting connector current with the corresponding current sensor."
findings.fix: In figures/FIG-2.md, insert after the connector current sensor paragraph: "A solid line leaves the lower side of the connector current sensor circle, runs downward, crosses the line from the control-pilot interface block once, then runs leftward beneath the control-pilot interface block and crosses the left side of the dashed rectangle below the isolated local bus, representing the sensing connection between the connector current sensor and the edge controller. It carries no reference numeral of its own and touches no block other than by that crossing of the dashed rectangle side." Make no change to the numeral list. In draft/08-detailed-description.md, amend the sentence to read: "The edge controller 106 is also coupled to the connector current sensor 124 of that connector channel by a sensing connection, and reads the connector current measured by the connector current sensor 124 over that connection." No claim amendment is required.
